title: Faith: trusting the one who promised
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. New wording, same facts: each claim is in the old film's captions or its 'differ' note, whose sources are in docs/work/elite/explorer-ledger.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, checked against client/public/bible/text/ by film/tools/write-script.py.

lines: Faith, in the Bible's sense, is trust in God and in what he has promised. It's not a leap in the dark, and it doesn't grow stronger the less evidence it has.
It's the answer a person gives to someone who has spoken and has proved reliable.

scripture.text: Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see.

lines: Abraham is the pattern. Old and childless, he was told his family would be like the stars, and he believed, centuries before the law.
Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
The same Abraham also doubted and schemed. Biblical faith is not a flawless mood. It's reliance that is tested and deepened.

scripture.text: Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.

lines: In the Gospels, faith is not a force the believer generates. It's reliance on Jesus himself, which is why a mustard seed of it is enough.
Its strength was never in the believing. It's in the one believed.

scripture.text: Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith

lines: A father brought his suffering son to Jesus, and prayed one of the most honest prayers in the Gospels.
I do believe; help my unbelief!
His faith was mixed and struggling, and Jesus answered it. Doubt brought to Jesus is still coming to Jesus.

scripture.text: I do believe; help my unbelief!

lines: Faith grows the way trust between persons grows: by hearing and remembering what the other has said and done.
That's why Scripture keeps retelling the exodus, and why Paul ties faith to hearing the word.

scripture.text: Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.

lines: The Bible's word for faith is also its word for faithfulness, so trust doesn't stay private. It obeys, endures, and keeps its promises.
Churches describe the link between faith and works in different words, and none of them teaches that faith earns salvation. This film takes no side.

scripture.text: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.

lines: Hebrews eleven is a list of people who acted on what God had said without seeing the outcome. Many died still waiting.
Faith doesn't deny the darkness. It holds to the one who has spoken in it, and walks on.
For we walk by faith, not by sight.

scripture.text: For we walk by faith, not by sight.

lines: Its strength is in the one believed.
